rows.response_text: The Bible emphasizes the power of words, stating that they can do much more than just convey information. According to the Bible, words have the ability to destroy a person's spirit and even incite hatred and violence (passage 1). This power is not to be used lightly or maliciously, as shown in Proverbs 15:4 and Romans 12:17-18 where the use of gentle words and avoidance of evil are encouraged (passage 2). Therefore, the Bible warns about the destructive potential of words and encourages their respectful use.
rows.source_text:
{"passages":"passage 1:Question: What does the Bible say about the power of words?. Answer: Words are not simply sounds caused by air passing through our larynx. Words have real power. God spoke the world into being by the power of His words (Hebrews 11:3), and we are in His image in part because of the power we have with words. Words do more than convey information. The power of our words can actually destroy one’s spirit, even stir up hatred and violence.

passage 2:Proverbs 15:4 ESV / 101 helpful votes. A gentle tongue is a tree of life, but perverseness in it breaks the spirit. Psalm 19:14 ESV / 95 helpful votes. Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer. Romans 12:17-18 ESV / 85 helpful votes. Repay no one evil for evil, but give thought to do what is honorable in the sight of all.

passage 3:Respectfully Destroying a Bible. 1  1. Show respect to the Bible. The Bible itself doesn't contain any special instructions for its own disposal. 2  2. Bury the Bible. One way to dispose of an old Bible is to return it to the Earth with a respectful burial. 3  3. Cremate the Bible.
